content:
ana: heads-up — Paradigm dedicated pool (eu-west-1) started spiking 429s around 08:12 UTC. We saw a scale-up to 6 nodes, then a scale-down to 3 within 90s; customers reported p95 text-gen latency > 3s. Anyone picking this up?

mike: saw the alert, grabbing autoscaler logs now. pinging @jordan

sre-bot: [alert] tenant=Paradigm pool=dedicated-eu-west severity=warning metric=throttle_429s rate=41/m

jordan: i see the same. autoscaler events show: 
```
2026-02-18T08:11:58Z scale.up reason="cpu_spike" from=3 to=6
2026-02-18T08:12:50Z scale.down reason="cpu_below_threshold" from=6 to=3
```
Looks like short CPU bursts triggered scale up, then rapid cooldown triggered scale down before traffic fully stabilized.

sophia: any noisy neighbors? could be tenant batch jobs breathing on GPUs. I pulled gpunode metrics: memory_pressure spiked to 78% for 30s at 08:11.

mike: repro steps I'm running: hitting the pool with 200 concurrent small requests (seq_len ~ 64) and some larger batched jobs from the tenant. I see per-instance cpu oscillation. Curl to reproduce quick:
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rw-large","input":"hi"}' &
done
```
This reproduces the 429s locally for that tenant's pool within 2-3 minutes.

ana: config check — the pool cooldown is set to 90s (scale_down_cooldown_sec=90). Autoscaler uses instantaneous cpu > 70% threshold. Suggest increasing scale_down_cooldown to 600s and switch to a rolling_avg window=120s for the cpu metric.

jordan: agreed. also add hysteresis: require cpu > 70% for 30s before scale up, and cpu < 55% for 300s for scale down. That should prevent snapback.

support-ops: notifying Paradigm support. We should offer a mitigation: pin them to a slightly larger reserved pool for next 24h or enable burst_capacity.

sophia: note — KV cache warmup isn't the issue here; it's raw compute spikes from tenant batch tasks. If we can tag batch jobs and route them to burst-nodes with isolation, that would help.

mike: i updated a test autoscaler policy in staging: 
```
scaler.policy = {
  scale_up: {threshold: 70, duration_sec: 30},
  scale_down: {threshold: 55, duration_sec: 300},
  cooldown_sec: 600,
  smoothing_window_sec: 120
}
```
Applying to eu-west staging pool now.

ana: good. after staging bake, we should push to prod and open a temporary canary route to 2% of traffic for 1h.

jordan: i'll run the canary for Paradigm and monitor p95 + 429 rate. If stable after 40m, we roll to 100%.

sre-bot: [deploy] autoscaler-policy updated in staging by mike at 08:38 UTC

support-ops: Paradigm notified, they accepted temporary reserved pool. ETA for change = 35m.

ana: thanks everyone. follow-ups: (1) prod rollout plan (2) postmortem draft if we see recurrence (3) investigate tenant batch scheduling to avoid shared GPU pressure.

mike: adding docs note to runbooks: "snapback scaling" mitigation steps + commands.

jordan: i'll post results in #incidents if canary shows improvement.

ana: closing loop for now. :thumbsup:
